              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: What to locate in the image.
      type: object
      required:
        - type
      title: BoxQuestion
      description: >-
        A question that locates what its instructions describe in the request's
        image. Requests with box questions must send the header
        TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true.
    NoulAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: noul
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a yes/no answer.
          examples:
            - noul
        noul:
          type: number
          title: Noul
          description: >-
            Probability of a yes answer or a true statement, from 0 to 1. Values
            near 1 favor yes or true, values near 0 favor no or false, and
            values near 0.5 indicate uncertainty.
          examples:
            - 0.98
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - noul
      title: NoulAnswer
      description: The probability of a yes answer or a true statement.
    ChoiceAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: choice
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a selection from the requested choices.
          examples:
            - choice
        choice:
          type: string
          title: Choice
          description: >-
            The name of the choice with the highest probability among the
            question's criteria.
          examples:
            - angry
        confidence:
          type: number
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence in the selected choice, from 0 to 1. Higher values
            indicate greater certainty; use lower values to flag uncertain
            selections for review.
          examples:
            - 0.9
        probabilities:
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
          type: object
          title: Probabilities
          description: >-
            Probability of each choice in criteria, keyed by choice name, from 0
            to 1. Shows how likely the alternatives are; values sum to
            approximately 1.
          examples:
            - angry: 0.8
              calm: 0.1
              excited: 0.1
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - choice
        - confidence
        - probabilities
      title: ChoiceAnswer
      description: >-
        The selected choice, confidence, and probabilities for a choice
        question.
    ScoreAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: score
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a rating against the requested score levels.
          examples:
            - score
        score:
          type: number
          title: Score
          description: >-
            Expected score: the probability-weighted average of the rubric
            levels. May fall between integer levels.
          examples:
            - 1.7
        confidence:
          type: number
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence in the score, from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate greater
            certainty; use lower values to flag uncertain ratings for review.
          examples:
            - 0.9
        legend:
          additionalProperties:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - additionalProperties: true
                type: object
              - items: {}
                type: array
            x-accepts: string | object | array
          type: object
          title: Legend
          description: >-
            The requested criteria mapped to their score levels, so you can
            interpret the score.
          examples:
            - '0': Can wait
              '1': Needs attention this week
              '2': Needs attention today
        probabilities:
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
          type: object
          title: Probabilities
          description: >-
            Probability of each score level, from 0 to 1, using the same keys as
            legend. Shows how likely the alternatives are; values sum to
            approximately 1.
          examples:
            - '0': 0.1
              '1': 0.1
              '2': 0.8
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - score
        - confidence
        - legend
        - probabilities
      title: ScoreAnswer
      description: >-
        An expected score with its rubric, confidence, and score-level
        probabilities.
    BoxAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: box
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a box answer.
          examples:
            - box
        box:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/BoxCoordinates'
          description: >-
            The box's edges as fractions of image height and width, from 0 to 1.
            Each coordinate is the expected value of its edge's predicted
            position.
          examples:
            - bottom: 0.66
              left: 0.19
              right: 0.68
              top: 0.2
        confidence:
          anyOf:
            - type: number
            - type: 'null'
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence for the given box, from 0 to 1, with 1 being more
            confident. Null when the model does not provide confidence.
          examples:
            - null
            - 0.9
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - box
        - confidence
      title: BoxAnswer
      description: A located box with normalized edge coordinates and confidence.
    NoulCriteria:
      properties:
        'true':
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: 'True'
          description: What counts as a yes answer.
          examples:
            - The message is unsolicited advertising.
        'false':
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: 'False'
          description: What counts as a no answer.
          examples:
            - The message is a legitimate conversation.
      type: object
      title: NoulCriteria
      description: Criteria defining what counts as a yes or no answer.
    BoxCoordinates:
      properties:
        top:
          type: number
          title: Top
          description: >-
            Top edge of the box, as a fraction of image height from the top
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.2
        bottom:
          type: number
          title: Bottom
          description: >-
            Bottom edge of the box, as a fraction of image height from the top
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.66
        left:
          type: number
          title: Left
          description: >-
            Left edge of the box, as a fraction of image width from the left
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.19
        right:
          type: number
          title: Right
          description: >-
            Right edge of the box, as a fraction of image width from the left
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.68
      type: object
      required:
        - top
        - bottom
        - left
        - right
      title: BoxCoordinates
      description: >-
        Normalized box edges. Vertical coordinates are measured from the top of
        the image; horizontal coordinates are measured from the left.
  securitySchemes:
    HTTPBearer:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer

I need to read all source files in op-llm line by line.

I'll check a prior receipt for the expected format and model context limits. I'll measure file sizes with wc -l before reading the crate's Cargo.toml, scripts, SPEC.md, and src/*.rs.

I'll check git status for prior edits in op-llm. I'll read models.md for context limits. The rename targets are tched, tched_router, tched_bridge, Tched, TCHED, and 3tched. Exact lookups and policy names will be excluded. Environment keys, D-Bus paths, and socket paths will not be renamed.

I will send all candidate spans to JEV for judgment rather than pre-filtering them myself. I will leave "threetched" unchanged if it matches the pinned schema. I will not rename real ZeroClaw 0.8.4 commands. The line-by-line requirement means reading the files personally, not that I cannot use a script to extract candidate spans afterward.

I will read all files directly rather than grep-hunting. I have enough context from the OpenAPI spec to skip the noul criteria page. I am designing a two-part question for each candidate occurrence.

The two-part question for each candidate is now defined. One score checks if the occurrence is the removed hand-rolled bridge. The other checks if it is the schema label that should become threetched. A rename will proceed only if both scores are at least 0.7 and there is no strong contradiction.

The rename rule is now a simple OR. If either JEV score reaches 0.7 or higher, the identifier becomes threetched. If both scores are 0.3 or lower, the occurrence is rejected and left unchanged. In all other cases the identifier is left as-is.

A third noul will check if the token is a real ZeroClaw 0.8.4 command name. Exact command matching against help output is code-level work, not JEV judgment. Environment keys, D-Bus paths, and socket paths are structural identifiers that code can detect, but I will still provide JEV with surrounding context so it can judge them.

Code must override JEV and refuse to rename environment keys, D-Bus paths, or socket paths even if JEV scores them high. The receipt will record these exclusions by policy. The instruction to edit files immediately targets identifier tokens specifically, not prose words in comments or documentation.

I must avoid renaming identifiers that are already threetched. The filesystem name 3tched-fs is our own, not the removed bridge, so JEV should reject or abstain on that token. Our schema label may also appear as string literals such as plugin IDs.

`tched_router` is the whole identifier to rename, not `threetched_router`. The plugin ID may become `threetched` if JEV marks it as our schema label. Environment variables like `TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_*` must stay unchanged.
I’ll match the existing receipt style, then read every `op-llm` file in order.

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Models

Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first [System One model](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md). Every model on this page is served by the same endpoint, `POST /v1/systemone`. The request's `model` field selects which one handles the call; see the [API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) for the full request shape.

## Current models

| | Jev 1.14 | Jev 1.13 |
| :- | :- | :- |
| Model ID | `jev-1.14.0` | `jev-1.13.0` |
| Price (per Btok / per Mtok) | \$42 / \$0.042 | \$42 / \$0.042 |
| Context length | 64k per-request / 32k per-question | 64k per-request / 32k per-question |
| Input | Text | Text |

Jev 1.14 is the newest Jev release, available from October 14, 2026.

* **Price:** You pay per input token. Output tokens are free. A Btok is a billion tokens and an Mtok is a million tokens.
* **Context length:** Two limits, the per-request context and the per-question context. See [Context length](#context-length). To raise both, see [Long context](#long-context).
* **Input:** Jev reads natural-language text, sent as a string, a JSON object, or an array of text values. It does not accept audio or video. Convert those into text or structured fields before you send them as `state`. See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md) for the shapes `state` accepts.

## Context length

Jev ingests the `state` once and evaluates every question against it in parallel. A request has to fit two context limits:

* **Per-request context** (`per_request_context`): the `state` plus all questions combined.
* **Per-question context** (`per_question_context`): the `state` plus any one question.

There is no separate limit on the number of questions in a request. Any number of questions is allowed as long as the request fits both limits. See [Speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md) for packing many questions into one request, and [Jev 1.13 jaggedness](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md) for how accuracy shifts as the state grows.

To raise both limits, see [Long context](#long-context).

### Long context

Long context is off by default and works on both Jev 1.14 and Jev 1.13. To turn it on, send the `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true` header with each request that needs it. With the header, the per-request context and the per-question context are both 262k tokens. Requests without the header keep the default limits in the table above.

```bash theme={null}
curl https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: *** $TYPESAFE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-latest",
    "state": "<a long contract, transcript, or record>",
    "questions": {
      "has_termination_clause": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does the `state` include a clause that lets either party end the agreement early?"
      }
    }
  }'
```

Long context costs the same per token as any other request. It is slower and less accurate than staying within the default limits, so turn it on only for requests that need it.

## Rate limits

Rate limits are set per organization. Your organization's current limits are in the [developer console](https://console.typesafe.ai/rate-limits).

Limits are measured in tokens per second and requests per second. A request over either limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Our [client SDKs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk.md) retry these requests by default, waiting longer between each attempt, and follow the `retry-after` header when the response includes one. If you call the HTTP API directly, see [Handling rate limits](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/errors.md#handling-rate-limits).

Higher limits are available on custom and enterprise plans. Contact [sales@typesafe.ai](mailto:sales@typesafe.ai).

## Aliases

An alias is a model name that points to a versioned model ID. Send it in the `model` field the same way you send a model ID.

| Alias | Points to | Meaning |
| :- | :- | :- |
| `jev-latest` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent stable, official release. The default in our client SDKs, and the name the examples in these docs use. |
| `jev-preview` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent release, official or not. Moves ahead of `jev-latest` when a preview build is available. |

> [!WARNING]
>
> `jev-preview` currently points to the same model as `jev-latest`. There is no preview build available right now.

An alias moves when a new release ships, so its answers can change without any change to your code. Each response's `model` field gives the versioned ID that answered, so you can log which model produced each result. If you have tuned confidence thresholds against one version, send that version's ID instead of the alias, and switch to the new version when you are ready.

## Customizing Jev

Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data. It is trained with [RLCD](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/machine-learning-primer.md) to return calibrated decisions, and the same weights serve every account. You shape its answers to your domain through the request rather than through per-account weights:

* Put your proprietary content, records, and reference material in the `state` field. See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md).
* Encode your domain rules and boundary cases in the `instructions` and `criteria` of each question. See [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md) and [Advanced: structure](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced.md).
* Decompose broad judgments into atomic questions and combine the outputs in code. See [Composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) and the [AutoResearch cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md) for training a downstream classical model on Jev's probabilities.

## Language support

Jev accepts natural-language text. English is the primary training language and where accuracy is currently best. Other languages, including CJK scripts, are handled but not equally well; test on your own content before relying on Jev for a non-English workload, and pay close attention to [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md) when routing.

## Data handling

Jev is not trained on customer requests or responses. See [Legal](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal.md) for the Data Processing Agreement, the Privacy Policy, and details on zero data retention (ZDR) for enterprise customers.

## Listing models

`GET /v1/models` returns the names your account can send in the `model` field, each with a description and a release date. It currently lists the aliases. Versioned IDs such as `jev-1.14.0` are accepted by the `model` field whether or not they appear in the list.

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: *** $TYPESAFE_API_KEY"
```

```python Python theme={null}
from typesafe_sdk import TypeSafeClient

with TypeSafeClient() as client:
    for model in client.models.list().models:
        print(model.name, model.release_date, model.description)
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { TypeSafeClient } from "@typesafe-ai/sdk";

const client = new TypeSafeClient();
const models = await client.models.list();
for (const model of models) {
  console.log(model.name, model.release_date, model.description);
}
```

**models** `array` *required*

One entry per model or alias.

**properties**

**name** `string` *required*

The model ID or alias, as accepted by the `model` field.

**description** `string` *required*

What the model is for.

**release\_date** `string` *required*

When the model or alias was released.

See the [Python](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/api/clients/sync.md#typesafe_sdk.Models.list) and [JavaScript](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript/api/interfaces/Models.md) SDK references for the full method signatures.

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Noul

> A Noul question asks the TypeSafe model to evaluate a yes/no question and return the probability that the answer is yes.

Use a Noul when the answer is yes or no. For example, does this message ask for a refund, does this resume mention distributed systems, does this comment contain personal data. If the answer is one of several options, use a [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md). If it's a position on a spectrum, use a [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score.md). [Choose a question type](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives#choose-a-question-type) compares all three.

A Noul answer is a single number representing the probability that the answer is yes where 0 means no and 1 means yes.

## Request structure

The POST request body to the [TypeSafe API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) has the same three top-level fields as any other question type: `state`, which is the content to evaluate; `model`; and `questions`. Each Noul question has the following fields:

* `type`: Always `"noul"`.
* `instructions`: The yes/no question the model answers, or a statement for it to judge.
* `criteria`: Optional. An object with `true` and `false` descriptions of what a yes and a no mean.

Below is a request where the state is a support message and the two questions are whether the customer wants a person and whether they have contacted support before:

Try it in the Playground →

You choose the question ids, `is_human_escalation` and `is_repeat_contact` here. The ids are not sent to the model. Each answer is returned under the same id. The first question relies on `instructions` alone. The second adds `criteria` to say what counts as a yes and what counts as a no.

With the [Python SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python.md), the same questions are `Noul` objects:

```python theme={null}
from typesafe_sdk import Noul, NoulCriteria, TypeSafeClient

with TypeSafeClient() as client:
    response = client.system_one(
        model="jev-latest",
        state="I have asked three times now. Can I please just talk to a real person?",
        questions={
            "is_human_escalation": Noul(
                instructions="Is the customer asking for a human agent?",
            ),
            "is_repeat_contact": Noul(
                instructions="Has the customer contacted support about this before?",
                criteria=NoulCriteria(
                    true="Mentions a prior attempt, ticket, or that they have asked before",
                    false="No sign of any previous contact",
                ),
            ),
        },
    )

    print(response.answers["is_human_escalation"].noul)
    print(response.answers["is_repeat_contact"].noul)
```

The `system_one` method and the `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` endpoint are both named after [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md), TypeSafe's AI model. [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md) covers where to use it in your code.

If you're using a coding agent, install the [TypeSafe agent skill](https://docs.typesafe.ai/agent-skill.md#installation) first so it knows the request and response shapes.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `instructions` can be a string, an object, or an array. Start with a string. Use an object when the question needs data alongside it, such as a record to compare the state against, or when part of the question is built by your code. [Use structure in the questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md#use-structure-in-the-questions) explains when structure helps, and [the example below](#structured-instructions) shows it with questions built in code.

## Response structure

The response has one entry in `answers` per question, under the ids from the request:

```json theme={null}
{
  "model": "jev-1.13.0",
  "answers": {
    "is_human_escalation": {
      "type": "noul",
      "noul": 0.99
    },
    "is_repeat_contact": {
      "type": "noul",
      "noul": 0.93
    }
  },
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": 360,
    "output_tokens": 39
  }
}
```

Both answers here are close to 1. The customer says "talk to a real person", so `is_human_escalation` is 0.99. "I have asked three times now" matches the `true` description of `is_repeat_contact`, so it is 0.93.

## Reading a Noul

The number is the answer and the certainty in one. A value near 1 is a strong yes. A value near 0 is a strong no. A value near 0.5 means the model gives yes and no similar probability.

The table below shows recorded `jev-1.13.0` answers to the `is_human_escalation` question for different customer messages:

| State | `noul` |
| - | - |
| Thanks, that fixed it! | 0.02 |
| How do I reset my password? | 0.07 |
| I need this sorted today, whatever it takes. | 0.26 |
| Are you a bot? | 0.40 |
| Is there any way to speak to someone about my invoice? | 0.84 |
| I have asked three times now. Can I please just talk to a real person? | 0.99 |

The first two and the last two are clear. "I need this sorted today" is urgent but never asks for a person, and gets 0.26. "Are you a bot?" hints at wanting a human without asking for one, and the model splits almost evenly at 0.40. Both are the kind of message where a decision needs to be made based on a threshold in your code.

There is no separate `confidence` value for a Noul, unlike a [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md) or a [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score.md). A Noul's probability distribution has only two outcomes, yes and no, so the single `noul` value describes it completely. | Candidate | Noul: "Is the candidate strong in Python?" | Score: "How much Python experience does the candidate have?" |

content.text:
Prior edits already renamed a Cargo.toml comment from tched_router to "captured threetched plugin".

schema.rs was deleted and lib.rs no longer exports it. graph_turn_reminder.rs still contains the `3tchedFS` string literal. The owner naming distinction specifies `3tched-fs` as the filesystem package name.

`3tchedFS` is our filesystem name, not the removed bridge or schema label. I should ask JEV to judge whether this `3tched` token refers to the removed hand-rolled bridge or our schema label, since AGENTS.md already clarifies that `3tchedFS` is the filesystem.

The Cargo.toml comment already reads threetched, so it will be left unchanged. I am now scanning the remaining files systematically for any leftover tokens, including tched, tched_router, tched_bridge, Tched, TCHED, 3tched, and threetched. I also need to check whether patched contains the substring tched.

"patched" and "matched" do not contain the substring "tched". Only "threetched" and "3tched" include it as a suffix.

Already-correct threetched occurrences will be left unchanged. They do not need to go to JEV for judgment.
